result.text:
If you're having issues connecting to a Wi-Fi network, or are experiencing slow Wi-Fi speeds on your iPhone, there are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the issue.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Confirm your Wi-Fi connection
Turn off Connectivity Assist
Restart your iPhone
Remove VPN profiles
Test your connection with other devices
Reset your network settings

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Wi-Fi.
notes:
Note: 

Using Wi-Fi can deplete your battery power faster than your carrier network connection.

steps.text: Tap or slide the Wi-Fi switch to ON.
notes:
Note: 

To turn off your Wi-Fi, tap or slide the Wi-Fi switch to OFF.

steps.text: Select a network to join.
notes:
Note: 

Wi-Fi hotspots may have security limitations. If necessary, enter a password and tap Join.

steps.text: Tap the Info icon beside your Wi-Fi network.
From this screen, you can perform a variety of actions to manage your Wi-Fi connection:
notes:
Note:
Forget this Network - Select this option to remove the network from your device. You can re-add it later, but will need to enter its security information again.
Private Wi-Fi Address - Reduce tracking from other devices on this Wi-Fi network by enabling a Fixed or Rotating Wi-Fi address.
Auto-Join - When this option is enabled, your iPhone will always try to connect to this network when it's in range.
Forget this Network - Select this option to remove the network from your device. You can re-add it later, but will need to enter its security information again.
Private Wi-Fi Address - Reduce tracking from other devices on this Wi-Fi network by enabling a Fixed or Rotating Wi-Fi address.
Auto-Join - When this option is enabled, your iPhone will always try to connect to this network when it's in range.

result.text:
Within the Settings app, take a moment to confirm that your iPhone is connected to a Wi-Fi network. A blue checkmark will appear next to your active connection within your Wi-Fi settings. If you don't see one, tap on an available Wi-Fi network and attempt to connect. (Make sure your iPhone's Airplane Mode isn't on.)
Note: If you're successfully connected to Wi-Fi, but you're getting a "No Internet Connection" message, there may be an issue with your Wi-Fi router/gateway that you'll need to troubleshoot. Apple also maintains a list of recommended settings for Wi-Fi routers you'll want to review.
